where: Section 1, last paragraph of the definitions
problem: The sentence "The absolutely convergent series Σ1/n² and Σ1/2n sit inside the convergent family" writes the geometric series as Σ1/2n, with no exponent on the 2. Read in the natural way, Σ1/(2n) is half the harmonic series and diverges, so the sentence then declares a divergent series absolutely convergent. The figure writes Σ1/2ⁿ correctly, but the body text does not.
fix: Write Σ1/2ⁿ (or Σ(1/2)ⁿ) and add: this is geometric with ratio 1/2, so it converges. Note that Σ1/(2n) is a different series and diverges.

problem: "1/(n+1)1/2" and "Σm=2∞ 1/m1/2" use 1/2 as an exponent but print it on the baseline, so they can be read as multiplying by one half. The same happens in Section 2 with "Σ1/np" for the p-series.
fix: Keep the exponent raised or reuse the square root: |an| = 1/√(n+1) = 1/(n+1)<sup>1/2</sup>, and Σ<sub>m=2</sub>∞ 1/m<sup>1/2</sup>. In Section 2 write Σ1/n<sup>p</sup>.

problem: "Some syllabi say “convergence with absolute values” for absolute convergence" is not a recognised alternative name in standard texts; a student may take it as a term to reproduce in an exam.
fix: Delete the sentence, or replace it with the standard equivalent wording: some books write “Σan converges absolutely” instead of “Σan is absolutely convergent”.

where: Section 1 formula box and definitions, Section 2 worked list
problem: The formula is printed with subscripts (Σ|a<sub>n</sub>|) but the text beside it writes "an", "|an|", "aN", "Σn=1N |an|" on the baseline. On a phone these read as products, so the definitions of an and AN are hard to follow.
fix: Use <sub> consistently for every index in the chapter: a<sub>n</sub>, |a<sub>n</sub>|, a<sub>N</sub>, A<sub>N</sub> = Σ<sub>n=1</sub><sup>N</sup> |a<sub>n</sub>|.
